chunks: One of our companions, from Ali ibn al-Hasan al-Taymuli, from Ali ibn Asbaat, from Muhammad ibn Ali ibn Ja'far, who said:
who said: Al-Mamun asked Al-Reza (peace be upon him) about the saying of Allah, the Mighty and Majestic:
Do not drive them out of their houses, nor should they themselves go forth, unless they commit an open indecency

He said: It means by the 'open indecency', if she hurts the family of her husband. So when she does that, so if he so desires to exit her from before the completion of her waiting period, so he can do it.
ai.seo_question: What constitutes 'open indecency' in the context of a wife being driven out of her home according to Shia jurisprudence?
ai.summary: Recorded in Al-Kafi, this narration from Imam al-Rida (AS) during the Abbasid era clarifies that 'open indecency' (fahisha mubinnah) in Surah At-Talaq specifically denotes causing harm to the husband's household, thereby granting the husband the right to evict her before the iddah concludes. This interpretation underscores the Shia jurisprudential emphasis on mutual rights and the specific conditions under which a wife's residence rights are suspended during divorce proceedings.

en.hubeali: One of our companions, from Ali Bin Al Hassan Al Taymuly, from Ali Bin Asbaat, from Muhammad Bin Ali Bin Ja’far who said,
‘Al-Mamoun asked Al-Reza<sup>asws</sup> about the Words of Allah<sup>azwj</sup> Mighty and Majestic
[65:1] Do not drive them out of their houses, nor should they themselves go forth, unless they commit an open indecency

, he<sup>asws</sup> said: ‘It Means by the ‘open indecency’, if she hurts the family of her husband. So when she does that, so if he so desires to exit her from before the completion of her waiting period, so he can do it’.
en.sarwar: 2. Certain persons of our people have narrated from Ali ibn al-Hassan al-Taymuliy from Ali ibn Asbat from Muhammad ibn Ali ibn Ja‘far who has said the following: “
Once al-Ma’mun asked al-Rida’, ‘Alayhi al-Salam, about the words of Allah, most Majestic, most Glorious, ‘. . .
you must not send them out of their homes and they must not go out except if they commit an open indecent act’
He (the Imam) said, . . ‘open indecent act’, is a reference to her troubling the family of the man. If she did he can send her out, if he wants, before the end of her waiting period.’”
